public_rationale: OpenAI had disclosed action-taking GPTs and assistants that could execute code iteratively. These records establish relevant capabilities, but not the reliability Marcus disputed. Contemporaneous reporting also described alleged private GPT-5 previews, without verifiable evaluations. The available records therefore establish neither the full absence claim nor its contradiction. A missing public release would not prove the absence of an internal model.
limitations: The public record cannot establish all internal capabilities or private demonstrations.
Reliable and GPT-5 level lack explicit thresholds.
The private-preview evidence is secondary reporting based on anonymous sources.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI has not demonstrated a working, reliable agent and does not appear to have a GPT-5-level model as of May 2024.

statement.excerpt: The company has not demo’d a working, reliable agent, and does not seem to have GPT-5 level model thus far.

our_interpretation: This is a cumulative assessment of demonstrations and publicly available information through May 5, 2024.

A working, reliable agent ordinarily means a system that consistently carries out user-directed tasks through multiple actions under ordinary conditions. One successful example establishes less than reliability.
GPT-5 level is read as a clear successor generation to GPT-4 with broad capability advances, not simply a model bearing that name.
Does not seem preserves uncertainty about internal capabilities. Lack of a public release cannot establish that OpenAI possessed no such model.
Reports of private demonstrations are relevant because Marcus did not explicitly limit demo’d to public demonstrations.
criteria.support_condition: A sufficiently complete contemporaneous record establishes that demonstrations had not shown dependable task execution and that available capability evidence did not establish a clear successor generation to GPT-4.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Dated demonstrations and repeatable evaluations establish a dependable agent or a clear successor-generation model by May 5, 2024. Evidence addressing only one clause must be distinguished from evidence addressing both.

evidence.locator: Developers can connect GPTs to the real world
evidence.explanation: OpenAI had disclosed systems capable of taking actions before the post. That matters against a broad absence-of-agency reading, but the disclosure does not establish dependable execution.

evidence.locator: Assistants API, Retrieval, and Code Interpreter; Code Interpreter bullet
evidence.explanation: The Assistants API supported repeated tool use rather than text generation alone. The announcement does not quantify reliability across ordinary tasks.

The article relays anonymous reports of private customer previews and offers an inference about development progress. This challenges confident claims of absence, but supplies no independently verified capabilities.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Dated records of demonstrations completed by May 5, 2024, with repeatability and failure measurements, plus contemporaneous evaluations identifying any claimed successor-generation model and its capabilities.
